skill.name: set-up-shopify-meta-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Set up Meta Ads bidding for paid repeat Shopify orders through Product Metrics. Check tracking and order classification, then create and select a custom conversion for repeat-order revenue or profit in Meta.
skill.summary: Configure and verify Meta conversion tracking for paid repeat Shopify orders.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance alerts describe normal setup and verification, and most backticks mark documentation or routine commands. The audit confirms risks from authenticated order reads, a remote MCP interface, mutable setup guides, and an unpinned installer. The workflow also exposes a token entry risk, broader event sharing, unverified browser links, and conflicting profit event guidance.

remediation.issue: The agent may solicit a Meta access token and pass it to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the verified Product Metrics app or a dedicated secret input. Remove instructions to request tokens in chat or pass them through visible tool arguments.

remediation.issue: The order checks request full JSON responses that can expose sensitive store data.
remediation.suggestion: Use a read-only classification endpoint or field projection. Confirm the store and time range, and return only the classification and delivery fields needed for the check.

remediation.issue: The remote MCP fallback permits operations based on a live index.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval to use the remote connector. Allow only reviewed operations and confirm the action, workspace, and property before each write.

remediation.issue: Remote guides and browser links can change outside the reviewed skill.
remediation.suggestion: Use bundled or revision-pinned guides. Treat remote content as reference data and validate browser destinations and redirects against trusted platform hosts before presenting them.

remediation.issue: The installer does not pin the package or the skill source revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed installer version and an immutable source commit, verify integrity, and require approval before installation.

remediation.issue: Connecting Meta can enable event sharing beyond returning customer conversions.
remediation.suggestion: Show the selected pixel, event types, matching fields, and consent settings before enabling delivery. Require approval for the full scope and skip unrelated channel setup.

remediation.issue: The main skill and the returning customer guide name different events for profit bidding.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the general profit example from this workflow. Verify the repeat-customer event and purpose rule before recommending the ad set change.

semantic_findings.title: Agent Solicits a Meta Access Token
semantic_findings.description: The workflow permits asking for a live Meta token and passing it directly to a command. This may expose the token in conversation history or tool traces.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill expressly permits the exception, and the Meta guide says an assistant must ask for the token. Neither defines a protected agent input.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Browser Handoff
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks the person to open a URL from a tool result. An unexpected destination could lead to a fraudulent login or authorization page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The browser handoff is explicit, but the skill does not require checking the destination host. No evidence found of a malicious URL in the bundled files.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Connection Enables Broader Event Sharing
semantic_findings.description: The repeat-order workflow directs users to enable a Meta destination. That destination also sends checkout events, general purchases, and consented matching data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide directs users to leave sending enabled and lists a broader payload. It does not require confirmation of that scope before enabling delivery.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Guidance Can Select the Wrong Conversion
semantic_findings.description: The main skill names the general order profit event, while the returning customer guide names the repeat-order profit event. Following the main skill could optimize a retention ad set for the wrong orders.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two files specify different event names and purpose filters. The choice matters when the merchant selects the ad set conversion.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Bidding for Repeat Shopify Orders
content.value_statement: A general purchase conversion does not distinguish first orders from repeat orders. Use Product Metrics to verify repeat-order events and choose a dedicated Meta conversion for a retention campaign.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status and identify unfinished Shopify or Meta tracking steps.
Review whether recent Shopify orders are classified as new, returning, or unknown.
Guide a repeat test order and verify that its event appears in Meta Events Manager.
Identify the repeat-order revenue or profit event and its required custom conversion filter.
Guide the merchant through ad set selection and report which delivery checks still need attention.
limitations: Live tracking requires a linked Shopify store, an active Product Metrics subscription, a configured Meta destination, and applicable shopper consent.
The merchant must handle Shopify and Meta admin steps, including creating the custom conversion and selecting it in the ad set.
The repeat-order profit event requires active additional costs and complete cost data for the order.
Past orders are not imported into Meta, and later refunds do not update these repeat-order events.

use_cases.title: Prepare a retention campaign
use_cases.description: Check whether Shopify and Meta tracking are ready before using repeat-order revenue as a bidding signal.

use_cases.title: Choose a repeat-order conversion
use_cases.description: Compare repeat-order revenue and profit events, then identify the matching conversion filter for one retention ad set.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing Meta events
use_cases.description: Check order classification, shopper consent, and Meta delivery when the expected conversion event is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Check setup readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my Shopify store and Meta destination are ready for repeat-order tracking. Do not change any settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a read-only check of the existing setup.

prompt_templates.title: Review order classification
prompt_templates.prompt: For my selected store, summarize how many of my last 20 orders were new, returning, or unknown. Omit customer details and order margins.
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm that recent orders are being classified as expected.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a repeat test order
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a paid repeat order in payment test mode. Help me verify its classification, consent, and revenue event in Meta Events Manager.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate the revenue event before creating a custom conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Plan profit bidding for one ad set
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my repeat-order profit event is ready. Confirm the event and purpose filter, then list the Meta changes for one retention ad set. Leave all settings unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a manual change after confirming cost coverage and event delivery.

output_examples.input: Why is the returning customer event missing from the Meta selector?
output: Meta has not received a returning customer event yet.
Use a test customer with a prior paid order and accept marketing and analytics consent for the test.
Check Test events in Events Manager, then clear the test event code before live delivery.

output_examples.input: My repeat-order revenue event arrived. What should I select in Meta?
output: Create a Purchase custom conversion for the returning customer revenue event and apply the returning customer purpose filter.
Use the event value and currency without setting a fixed value.
Select the custom conversion in one retention ad set and verify it after saving.

best_practices: Verify the Shopify store, Meta pixel, event types, and consent settings before enabling live delivery.
Enter the Meta access token directly in the verified Product Metrics app and keep it out of chat.
Verify with a consenting test customer, remove the test event code, and start with one retention campaign.
anti_patterns: Using a general purchase or profit conversion when the goal is to bid only on repeat orders.
Assuming an order without a linked Shopify customer can be classified as returning.
Leaving the test event code active after verification and expecting events to appear in live reporting.

faq.question: What counts as a returning customer order?
faq.answer: The order must be paid and linked to a Shopify customer with an earlier order. The earlier order can predate app installation.

faq.question: Can I bid on repeat-order profit instead of revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the repeat-order profit event when additional costs are active and the order has complete cost data.

faq.question: Why is the event missing from the Meta selector?
faq.answer: Meta lists the event only after it receives it. Check a paid repeat test order with marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Do I need to share my Meta token with the assistant?
faq.answer: No. Enter your Conversions API token directly in the verified Product Metrics app.

faq.question: Will the assistant update my ad set?
faq.answer: No. Create the custom conversion and select it in Meta yourself. The assistant can guide the steps and help verify the result.

faq.question: Does Product Metrics send past orders or revise refunded events?
faq.answer: No. Past Shopify orders are not imported into Meta, and later refunds do not revise the repeat-order conversion events.
